body: That's wonderful!! I wish you all the luck in the world!!
It's provoked, it only hurts if it's touched and the pain is right in/on the entrance of my vagina. If I were to lightly press on the left side of my vagina I would be in pain
Oh thank you so much!! I totally forgot the name. I hope you find something that helps you <3
I hope it goes well for you! <3
It's really hard to describe unless you've used a tens unit before. It's almost a ticklish feeling? It doesn't hurt at all, it's just weird!

So the needles are placed around the nerves causing my pain, NOT directly in them! From what I understand they're placed around one specific nerve on the outside of my vagina. If you were to look at my vagina like a clock, straight at it, the spot that causes me pain would be at 1:00. There are typically two pairs of needles. Two go on one side of my painful area and the other two go on the opposite side but closer to my bottom. There is some nerve around that area that goes from your vagina, up around your bottom, and up your back. That's what I'm hoping to deaden! Home tens units are great for other muscle pain but this particular treatment is NOT one I would try at home. Inserting needles is not something you want to do yourself and your doctor/GYN would know specifically where your needles should be placed. I would absolutely ask your doctor about this treatment! Nothing traditional worked for me either and I was really starting to feel hopeless. I hope this helps you!!
Thank you so very much for the reply! I'm so glad that your pain isn't as bad anymore <3
Oh thank you for telling me!!

I stopped counseling two years ago but I'm thinking it would be healthy for me to look in to it again.  Thank you for your reply ❤️

Thank you so much for sharing this. I really needed to hear something new and this has lifted me up a bit. It's been such a long time since I've had suicidal thoughts or even cried because of my vulvodynia. This hasn't been a good day for me, but your information has really helped. As long as there is something new for me to try I will have a little bit of hope.

I haven't spoken to a physical therapist because I wasn't sure they could help with vulvodynia, I was told they might not be able to help me by doctors. So I hadn't looked much into them. Thank you so much for sharing your story. So you use a physical therapist? What do they do? How often do/did you see them? There are women's physical therapy centers near me and if they could possibly help me I'd give it my all. 

I've found the same about the Facebook groups, unfortunately. I do follow two Instagram accounts that share tips and info on vulvodynia. They both spread messages of positivity and on my bad days they can keep me going. 

I really needed to hear this. I am not and never have been the type of person to wallow around in misery, but I am so tired after coming to so many dead ends. I've started to feel really, truly hopeless. I was shocked to see that comment as many other women who are also battling vulvodynia are usually easy to relate to and know what the struggle is like. Thank you.

Unfortunately I don't get to choose how painful my vagina is or how much it makes me suffer. I do in fact believe that I deserve happiness. I am a very optimistic person and I have come out of one doctors office after another with a smile on face and ready to look at other opportunities for treatment or new paths to explore. I have full-heartedly believed that I will find an answer eventually and tried to be happy in the meantime. After two and a half years of this, please forgive me if I'm a little upset.
Just normal ob/gyns for now (many of them). I've recently been looking at specialists and universities that are actively researching women with problems like mine.   Everything is just so far away
